To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Estonian television has become a commercial enterprise, which is not interested in promoting Estonian culture and values.
the Estonian television broadcasting market has been characterized by a lack of diversity, a lack of competition, and a lack of public service broadcasting.
the Estonian television has become more internationalized, more commercialized and more Americanized.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of the Estonian broadcasting landscape in the period of transition and the infl uence of European Union media regulation.
how the Estonian television broadcasting market has been shaped by the economic and legal conditions.
the Estonian television industry and the infl uence of the Broadcasting Act amendments from the years 2000 and 2001 on the television industry and the Estonian television programmes’ content.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Estonian broadcasting landscape has changed from a public broadcasting dominated to a private broadcasting dominated landscape, where the public service media has lost its leading position.
the Estonian broadcasting market has been shaped in a way that is not in accordance with the EU principles.

, despite the fact that the Estonian Broadcasting Act is in compliance with the European Union media regulations, it has not been successful in creating a television landscape that is in accordance with the Estonian cultural and social values.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the Estonian television broadcasting landscape has changed from the beginning of the 21st century, but the change has not been as radical as it was in the 1990s, when the Estonian television system had to adapt to a completely different environment.
the Estonian Broadcasting Act has not been able to create a balanced television landscape, where the interests of the audience and the state are taken care of.
the Estonian television is a commercialized, internationalized and Americanized medium.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, in order to increase the value of the Estonian content, the state should support and protect the national television channels and, at the same, time, it should be more strict towards the private television companies and their content.
in the conditions of small television market and liberal policy, the regulation of media is more important than ever.
, in the case of the small transition state, the media policy has to be based on the principles of transparency and openness, which would guarantee the public the right to know and to participate.
